data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"As n grows, the probability of reaching unanimous consensus tends to 1. The only locally stable mixed configurations are those where crossing edges form a matching and each vertex has at most one opposite-color neighbor; these are non-expanding cuts and are exponentially rare, with expected number exp(-c n). The process cannot reach them from a typical random initial coloring, so consensus occurs with probability 1-o(1).","counterconditions":[{"case":"If random 3-regular graphs contain exponentially many stable mixed configurations with large basins, the consensus probability would tend to 0.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the final cut size is \u0398(n) with high probability, the claim fails.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Random 3-regular graphs are expanders. Majority dynamics on expanders rapidly eliminates local disagreements. Stable mixed configurations require a matching of crossing edges, which is a non-expanding cut; such cuts are exponentially rare in random regular graphs. The initial random coloring has a positive density of vertices with two or three opposite-color neighbors, and the monotone decrease of cut size drives the system to the empty cut.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
